Thanks again for the onboarding session last week. We dumped a few more edge cases into our test harness overnight and noticed some differences in how Redwood's streaming endpoint emits structured outputs versus what our downstream processors expect.

Attached are: helios-current-output-schema-v2.json and the prompt set we used (helios-prompt-set-20261129.json). High level asks for the checkpoint call:
- Confirm event boundary semantics for streaming chunks (are tool call start/end events guaranteed?)
- Confirm preferred function-calling signature for our external tool adapter (we currently expect {name, args, context})
- Walk through a short canary rollout strategy (we prefer feature-flagged traffic at 5% then 25%)

Are you available today for a short alignment call (30m)? Prefer after 1pm PT.

Best,
Sara

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Schema alignment & streaming/tool calling checkpoint

Quick technical note ahead of the call — pulled from our staging test run against the attached schema:

Observed mismatches (high level):
- Helios expects an event_type enum with values ["utterance", "tool_call", "tool_result"]. Redwood streaming emits "chunk" + a nested function_call object when tool calling is used.
- Tool call args: Helios schema requires args to be a flat map of strings (key -> string). Examples in your prompt set contain nested objects which result in escaped JSON in the args field.
- Schema field names: Helios uses snake_case (patient_id), Redwood suggests camelCase (patientId) in recent runtime schemas.

Proposed short-term compatibility layer (non-breaking):
1) During streaming, emit explicit tool_call start and end markers as separate events: e.g. event_type: "tool_call_start", followed by payload events, then event_type: "tool_call_end". This gives downstreams deterministic parsing without waiting for KV closure.
2) Offer an optional serialization flag in the request: output_schema_mode="flatten-args" that will coerce nested args into flattened keys (patient_address.street -> patient_address_street) so Helios doesn't need to alter existing adapter immediately.
3) Provide a quick JSON crosswalk mapping file (camelCase <-> snake_case) as a deliverable in the canary.

I'll prepare example request/response snippets for the call; attaching a tiny sample inline for clarity:

Example event stream snippet (conceptual):
{
  "event_type": "tool_call_start",
  "tool": "med-search",
  "meta": { "request_id": "r-123" }
}
{
  "event_type": "tool_result",
  "tool": "med-search",
  "result": { "matches": 3 }
}

We'll cover implementation cost and token delta on the call.

—Dylan
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@helioshealth.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Schema alignment & streaming/tool calling checkpoint

Thanks, Dylan — that matches our errors. A few clarifications from our side before 1:30pm:
- We prefer explicit event_type markers, yes. Naming is flexible but we need start/end so our parser can resume mid-stream after reconnects.
- Flattening is acceptable as a temporary measure; final schema will stick to nested objects. Can you include a small transformation library or an example function we can copy into our adapter?
- For the canary we want a monitoring hook that sends parsing error counts to our Sentry project and also a token-usage delta to our billing contact (cc'd: Carlos).

I'll upload a revised prompt set with a couple of edge-case examples to the Drive link you mentioned and will keep the team on standby for the call.

Sara
